issues.description: Off-by-one logic bug in the inner loop. The code uses `for j in range(i, N): middle_set.add(A[j - 1])` and only computes the sum when `j > i`. That causes A[i-1] (an element of the left prefix) to be added to the middle set, producing incorrect distinct counts for every middle subarray. This yields wrong answers (example: the sample case is overcounted to 6 in an intermediate step) and must be fixed.

Algorithmic complexity is still O(N^2) in the worst case (nested loops over i and j, even if middle distinct counts are updated incrementally). With N up to 3×10^5 this will TLE in the intended judge environment. A fundamentally faster approach (near linear or N log N) is required for the problem constraints.

No tests or verification artifacts were provided in the workspace. There are no unit or integration tests that exercise correctness or performance (edge cases, large inputs). Add tests that include small samples, boundary cases and large random inputs to validate correctness and performance.
